title: Add RAG stage-runner and instrumented snippets kit
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a local RAG stage-runner and browser playground to examples for developer authoring and reproducible debugging. This is purely additive and intended for devs and solutions engineers.
description:
Summary: Introduce a lightweight 'stage-runner' for authoring and debugging RAG scenarios locally, plus an instrumented snippets kit that wires telemetry and stepwise assertions into examples. Motivation: teams repeatedly ask for a small, deterministic harness to step through RAG pipelines (retrieval -> decode -> tool-calls -> post-processing) and capture per-stage telemetry without running full cloud infra. This PR provides a CLI runner and a compact browser playground that replay the same pipeline with inline probes so developers and evaluators can iterate quickly.

What changed (high level):
- New examples/rag-stage-runner/ package with a small TypeScript CLI and a stage execution runtime. The runtime models a RAG flow as named stages and emits structured events for each stage boundary.
- Browser playground that loads the same pipeline YAML and visualizes stages with timings and emitted telemetry events for quick inspection.
- Instrumentation snippets that show recommended telemetry hooks (span names, event types, token counts) and step assertions for regression testing.
- Docs under docs/rag-authoring/ describing how to onboard the stage-runner, recommended telemetry schema, and example recorded traces.

Commits (summary):
- 1) scaffold: initial package and TS build config + README
- 2) runner: implement stage executor, event bus, and deterministic RNG for reproducible outputs
- 3) playground: add browser runner bundle and UI wiring to render stage timeline and events
- 4) instrumentation: add telemetry probe snippets and assertion examples + CI smoke workflow
- 5) docs: authoring guide and images, small copy edits after reviews

Files touched (high level):
- CLI: examples/rag-stage-runner/cli/* (entrypoint, stage executor, helpers)
- Browser: examples/rag-stage-runner/browser/* (playground UI and bundle)
- Templates & snippets: examples/rag-stage-runner/templates/*, snippets/* (YAML pipelines and instrumentation examples)
- Docs: docs/rag-authoring/guide-stage-runner.md and an illustrative PNG
- CI: small smoke workflow to exercise the CLI on PRs

How to try locally: (CLI)
- yarn --cwd examples/rag-stage-runner install && yarn --cwd examples/rag-stage-runner build
- node dist/cli/index.js run --pipeline examples/rag-stage-runner/templates/basic-pipeline.yaml --record traces/out.json
- The output includes a per-stage event stream and a deterministic run id for replay.

How to try the browser playground:
- yarn --cwd examples/rag-stage-runner install && yarn --cwd examples/rag-stage-runner start:playground
- Open http://localhost:5173, load the basic-pipeline.yaml, and click 'Run'. The UI shows a timeline, per-stage metrics, emitted events, and inline assertion failures if any.

Design notes and constraints:
- The stage-runner intentionally avoids calling remote backends by default; it includes stub adapters that mimic model and vector-store latencies. This keeps runs fast and reproducible for local dev.
- Instrumentation follows our recommended telemetry schema (trace_id, run_id, stage_name, token_count, duration_ms, success) so traces can be correlated with production logs. The docs include the schema and a suggested mapping to existing tracing pipelines.
- Assertions are plain JS/MD snippets that can be run as a lightweight smoke test; they are not a full test harness but are helpful for catching regressions before CI.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Samira Ortiz (reviewer): "Nice small surface area. Two requests: 1) include a short example showing how to map stage events to our tracing attributes, and 2) make the deterministic RNG seed configurable via CLI. Otherwise :+1:"
- Maya Chen (author reply): "Added tracing mapping section in docs and CLI flag --seed; updated examples to use seed 42 for recorded traces."
- Daniel Park (reviewer): "Playground looks useful; can we make the timeline show token-level deltas?"
- Maya Chen: "Added optional token-breakdown toggle in the UI; default is off to keep noise down."
- Ravi Menon (reviewer): "CI smoke workflow flaked on Windows runner once; switched to ubuntu-latest only and added a retry step for bundle build."

CI and checks: All checks passed on final push. The smoke workflow runs the CLI with the basic pipeline and validates the generated trace JSON against the schema. Lint: passes. Typecheck: passes. Browser bundle build: passes.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: developers may treat the stage-runner as a production simulator. Mitigation: README and docs clearly state this is a local debugging tool with stub adapters and not intended to emulate production latency or model randomness.
- Risk: telemetry schema drift. Mitigation: included schema and mapping to the platform's tracing attributes; added a small unit test to validate emitted event keys.

Checklist: 
- [x] Tests added for emitted event schema (smoke).
- [x] Docs updated with quickstart and tracing mapping.
- [x] Playground UI added and smoke-tested locally.
- [x] CI smoke workflow added.
- [x] Review approvals from 2+ reviewers.

Release notes: Adds a local RAG stage-runner and browser playground to examples for developer authoring and reproducible debugging. This is purely additive and intended for devs and solutions engineers.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after approvals (Samira Ortiz, Daniel Park) and green CI. Merge commit f3a9c6d7... created and deployment not required.

If you want to iterate further: suggested follow-ups are 1) add a 'recording' importer to surface production traces in the same UI, 2) add more example tool adapters for common connectors (S3, Postgres, small vector DB), and 3) add an official CI job that runs stage-runner smoke tests against release candidates.
